title: GPT-6 Astra Proves Sharp Topological Overlap & Bukh–Matoušek–Nivasch Conjecture in Every Dimension
aiSystem: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (with Claude Opus 5.5 assistance)
whyItMatters: Settles the 2011 Bukh–Matoušek–Nivasch conjecture by proving the exact topological overlap constant c_d = (d+1)!/(d+1)^(d+1) for every dimension d—discovered by GPT-6 Astra under Sergey Norin’s direction.
summary: McGill mathematician Sergey Norin posted a self-contained proof establishing that the topological and affine overlap constants of simplices coincide and equal exactly (d+1)!/(d+1)^(d+1) in every dimension d, confirming the 2011 Bukh–Matoušek–Nivasch conjecture and sharply improving Gromov’s celebrated 2010 topological overlap bounds. In his transparent AI disclosure, Norin explains that after directing GPT-6 Astra to abandon numerical optimization and unify his bramble lemma with Gromov’s method, Astra discovered a conceptual Morse-theoretic and homological proof in 3D that generalized immediately to all dimensions.
technicalHighlights: Proves c_d^top = c_d^aff = (d+1)! / (d+1)^(d+1) for every positive integer dimension d, matching the 2011 Bukh–Matoušek–Nivasch upper bound.
Combines descending chain fillings, relative-homology vanishing, Morse theory, and a novel Hessian eigenvalue lower bound on multilinear cocycle densities.
Exemplifies transparent human–AI mathematical collaboration: GPT-6 Astra found the core conceptual proof under Norin’s guidance, while Norin digested, verified, and restructured the full manuscript.
caveats: Unrefereed v1 arXiv preprint without a machine-checked Lean formalization; while Norin personally checked and rewrote every step over several weeks, formal peer review is pending.

scoreRationale.foundational: Determines the exact optimal constant in Gromov’s topological overlap theorem across every dimension, resolving a 15-year-old conjecture.
scoreRationale.ripple: Advances discrete geometry and combinatorial topology, and serves as a landmark case study of an LLM producing a genuinely conceptual, non-brute-force proof.
scoreRationale.verification: Clean, human-vetted manuscript by a leading combinatorialist (Sergey Norin), though unrefereed and not formally verified in Lean.
scoreRationale.velocity: Solved in all dimensions after human efforts had stalled at suboptimal 3D bounds matching Gromov’s 2010 estimates.
